title: Audio Library
description: GENERATED by tools/audio-pipeline — rewritten in full on every run, so nothing a human decided may be stored here (that is audio-review.schema.json's job, and reservations live in the shared asset registry). Singleton file: data/audio/library.json. What each source file physically is, how loud it measured, and exactly how it was processed into the file players download.

ffmpeg.description: The exact ffmpeg build that measured and encoded this library.

root.description: Where processed audio lives, relative to Foundry's user-data root.

id.description: Stable across renames, moves and re-downloads (matched by content, then by path). Reservations, review decisions and every authored cue point at this.

source.description: The file in audio/in-tray/, which the pipeline never modifies, moves or deletes.

durationSec.description: As the container CLAIMS. Not always true — see analysis.decodedDurationSec.

tags.description: Embedded metadata worth keeping: title, artist, album, genre, comment (sound libraries describe their own contents here), copyright.

analysis.description: EBU R128 loudness of the source, plus what decoding it actually produced.

maxShortTermLufs.description: Null for anything shorter than the 3-second window.

decodedDurationSec.description: How much audio actually decoded. A container header can be wrong.

proposal.description: The pipeline's own opinion, never a decision. A human confirms or overrules it in review.json.

reasons.description: Why it thinks so, in plain sentences — a proposal nobody can check is not reviewable.

encode.description: How the processed file was built. Null until it has been.

gainDb.description: Loudness normalisation, baked into the file.

gainCorrectionDb.description: A second-pass correction measured on the first encode (surround downmixes need one).

shortfallDb.description: How far under target it deliberately plays, to keep its peaks intact.

loop.description: The seamless-loop crossfade folded back into the file.

output.description: Measured from the processed file itself — the proof that it landed on target, not the intention that it would.
